title: Self-hosted connectivity audit heuristics and safeguard notes
content:
Overview:
This is a working sketch for heuristics, lightweight audit shapes, and approval gate guidance for self-hosted / customer-managed networking in Redwood Private deployments. Aim: provide a minimal safe set that reduces operations friction for customers while preserving auditability and compliance posture for enterprise buyers.

Problem statement:
- Customers run Private in VPCs or on-prem and want to maintain their network controls and audit trails while Redwood needs visibility for support, billing, and incident response.
- Existing proposals are heavy (full per-flow packet capture, long retention) which increases cost and customer resistance.
- Need approval gates for network changes (port openings, egress rules, NAT changes, route table updates) that balance speed and governance.

Goals:
- Define an audit log schema that captures intent and outcome for network operations without exposing sensitive customer payloads.
- Propose approval gate levels (auto-approve, ops-review, security-review) and triggers.
- Recommend default retention tiers and an opt-in extended retention flow.
- Provide an onboarding handoff checklist for SRE/solutions to reduce rework.

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: audit events emitted by Redwood agent, control-plane approval metadata, handoff checklist, default retention settings, approval policies templates.
- Out of scope: packet-level telemetry, SIEM ingestion backends (we'll provide formats but not integrations in this doc).

Proposed Audit Event Schema (minimal fields):
- event_id (uuid)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor (string: "redwood-agent" | "customer-admin" | redwood-staff email)
- actor_id (opaque id)
- action_type (string: e.g., "route-update,""security-group-change,""egress-rule-add,""nat-gateway-attach")
- target (string: resource identifier, e.g., vpc-abc123, subnet-foo)
- intent (string: freeform short description supplied by actor)
- before_snapshot (SHA256 or short fingerprint)  // not raw config
- after_snapshot (SHA256 or short fingerprint)
- outcome (enum: success | failed | pending | rolled_back)
- approval_policy_id (optional)
- approver_ids (list of strings)
- references (list of ticket ids/urls)
- retention_tier (enum: short|standard|extended)

Notes on schema choices:
- We intentionally avoid storing raw private routing tables or IP-level data; instead store fingerprints and delta descriptors to reduce PII/exposure.
- References should be used to point to customer-side tickets (they own the full config dump).

Approval Gate Levels (draft):
- Gate 0: Auto-approve (low-risk, e.g., tagging changes, non-firewall metadata)
- Gate 1: Ops-review (changes that affect connectivity but not external exposure: route table swaps within same AZ)
- Gate 2: Security-review (egress to internet, opening inbound ports, enabling public endpoints)
- Gate 3: Exec escalation (cross-account peering, long-lived external NATs, changes with >30m expected downtime)

Trigger heuristics (examples):
- If action_type in {"egress-rule-add","security-group-open_inbound"} => Gate 2
- If change affects more than N subnets or more than X instances (configurable thresholds) => Gate up one level
- If request origin is a redwood-staff automation token and lacks a ticket => fail fast (require human ticket)

Approval flow sketches:
- Customer-initiated change: customer opens ticket (link in references), triggers agent to emit 'pending' event -> Redwood console shows approval widget -> approver uses one-click approve or requests clarification -> once approved, control-plane executes and updates event to success/failed.
- Redwood-initiated maintenance (scheduled): pre-notify customer with a generated ticket and auto-escalate to Gate 1 for short maint windows.

Retention tiers:
- short: 30 days (default for dev/test customers)
- standard: 365 days (default for customers with SLA)
- extended: 7 years (opt-in, paid, for regulated customers)

Storage & Export:
- Events stored encrypted at rest in control-plane.
- Provide JSON-lines export endpoint per workload with per-event minimal fields.
- Include a signed manifest for exported batches (for audit integrity).

Onboarding / Handoff checklist (SRE <> customer):
- Confirm VPC CIDRs and list of peering connections
- Define change approvers and Slack/Email contact list
- Provide baseline config snapshot (customer keeps full config)
- Establish ticketing template (fields: intent, scope, rollback plan, maintenance window)
- Agree on retention tier and export cadence

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: customers expect raw flow logs — mitigation: document tradeoffs and offer a separate opt-in data pipeline for flow logs with clear SLA and cost-sharing.
- Risk: approval friction slows ops — mitigation: thresholds for auto-approval and role-based exceptions.
- Risk: audit event tampering — mitigation: append-only signed manifests and periodic attestations.

Open questions:
- Should we include non-IP resource attributes (e.g., security-group rules text) for a 90-day window for troubleshooting? (pros: faster debugging, cons: exposure)
- How to integrate with customer SIEMs (Splunk, SumoLogic)? Push vs pull? Initial target: provide S3-compatible export with presigned URLs.
- Policy UI: console-only vs API-first. Recommend both, but prioritize API for infra automation.

Implementation rough plan (next steps):
- Quick spike: implement minimal audit event producer in agent (2 engineer-weeks)
- Design: approval widget mockups + policy editor (1 PM + 1 design cycle)
- Pilot: 3 customers under standard retention for 3 months
- Iterate on schema and retention after pilot

TODO / action items:
- [ ] Align with legal on retention maximums (Maya)
- [ ] Draft SLA language for extended retention (Arjun)
- [ ] Wire up S3 export prototype (eng: Tomás)
- [ ] Create ticket template and add to docs (docs: Lena)

Notes-to-self:
- Keep examples concrete in the console mockups (show a 'before/after fingerprint' diff)
- Log sizes estimated: ~2k events/month per large customer => plan storage accordingly

References and related docs:
- See control-plane-audit-sampling-and-approval-proof-prd-notes.json (drive)
- Related: customer-network-handover-playbook-audit-scenarios.json

End of doc.
